## New Year in Rio and Iguazu in seven days

**This itinerary lasts seven days and six nights:** first come New Year's celebrations and sightseeing in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), followed by a domestic flight to the [Iguazu region](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and visits to the waterfalls on both sides of the border. The return flight home is planned from the Foz do Iguaçu area.

It is an option for travelers who want to celebrate New Year's Eve on Copacabana and see one of South America's best-known natural attractions without additional beach days. The [10-day New Year program](/brazil/tour/brazil-new-year-rio-iguazu-buzios-10-days/) continues with relaxation in Búzios. The [five-day Rio-only trip](/brazil/tour/rio-new-year-copacabana-christ-redeemer-sugarloaf/) does not involve flying to Iguazu.

## The first three days: festive Rio

On arrival day, travelers are met at the airport and transferred to their hotel, with time to rest. On December 31, the itinerary takes them to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado. After the excursion, there is time to prepare for the evening celebrations on Copacabana. Traditionally, people dressed in white gather on the beach, concerts take place and fireworks light up the ocean at midnight. A separate dinner or hotel celebration is an optional extra.

On January 1, the program includes the ascent to Sugarloaf Mountain via Urca and a tour of central Rio. The two viewpoints provide different panoramas: from Corcovado, neighborhoods set among mountains and beaches; from Sugarloaf, the bay and coastline.

During New Year's celebrations, city authorities restrict traffic around Copacabana. The exact transport timetable and pedestrian access arrangements for a particular year should be checked closer to the holiday. Excursion dates may be adjusted to reflect attraction opening schedules.

## Flight on January 2 and both sides of the falls

Day four is devoted to the flight from Rio to Foz do Iguaçu and hotel check-in. Day five covers the [Brazilian side of the waterfalls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), with panoramic viewing trails. Day six takes place on the [Argentine side](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), where visitors explore the upper and lower trails, the ecological train and the Devil's Throat area.

**Crossing the international border is part of the itinerary.** Required immigration documents depend on each traveler's passport. During high water, park management may close certain viewing areas; the itinerary does not guarantee access to every walkway.

Optional activities include the bird park for **$50** and Macuco Safari for **$130** per person. Both are charged separately. Day seven ends with a transfer to Foz do Iguaçu airport.

## Price, flights and travel pace

| Item | Itinerary details |
|---|---|
| Duration | 7 days / 6 nights |
| Cities | Rio, Foz do Iguaçu |
| Waterfalls | Both sides |
| Price | From $1791 |
| Departure airport | Foz do Iguaçu |

The package includes hotels, group excursions with a Russian-speaking guide and transfers with a driver. International and domestic flights, additional meals and drinks, tips, laundry and optional excursions are excluded.

When planning flights, remember that the journey home begins **in Foz do Iguaçu**, with no mandatory return to Rio. The itinerary is busy: each of the two national parks has a dedicated day. Iguazu is hot and humid in summer, so lightweight clothing, non-slip footwear and protection from spray for documents and electronics will be useful.

## Choosing between five, seven and ten days

For New Year's atmosphere in Rio and relaxation without changing hotels, consider the [five-day tour](/brazil/tour/rio-new-year-copacabana-christ-redeemer-sugarloaf/). For festive Rio and both sides of Iguazu, choose this week-long itinerary. For additional beach days in [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/) or another resort area, see the [10-day program](/brazil/tour/brazil-new-year-rio-iguazu-buzios-10-days/).

## Frequently asked questions about the seven-day program

### Does the tour visit the Argentine side of Iguazu?

Yes. The Argentine side is included on day six, after the Brazilian side on day five.

### Is there beach time after Iguazu?

No. The return flight home from Foz do Iguaçu is planned for day seven.

### Is the domestic flight included?

No. The Rio–Foz do Iguaçu flight is paid for separately.

### Are documents needed to enter Argentina?

Yes. Current entry requirements must be checked according to each traveler's citizenship and passport.

## Brazil group tour: nine days between Rio, Iguazu and São Paulo

This itinerary takes the group through [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [São Paulo](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/), in that order. The journey lasts **9 days and 8 nights**, with group pricing calculated for **40 participants plus one free-of-charge place (FOC)**. English-speaking guides are provided for the specified transfers and excursions. Domestic flights connect the cities, but the air tickets are paid for separately.

This route is designed for a large organized group looking to combine Rio's famous views, the natural attractions around the waterfalls and the urban sights of São Paulo. The main planning priority is to agree on the flights, meal program and accommodation package before finalizing the budget.

## What the group can see

| Days | Main program |
|---|---|
| 1–4 | Rio, Corcovado, Tijuca |
| 5–6 | Flight and Iguazu Falls |
| 7–9 | São Paulo and departure |

**Rio occupies the first four days.** After an airport welcome and a welcome dinner, the group enjoys [Sugarloaf Mountain and a city sightseeing tour](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/sugarloaf-rio-city-half-day-english/), followed by [Corcovado and Santa Teresa](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/corcovado-santa-teresa-half-day/). Another half-day is devoted to [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/) and a [guided walk in the tropical forest](/brazil/tijuca-national-park/tijuca-forest-half-day-lunch/). Each of these days lists a half-day excursion; the remaining hours should be considered separately, without assuming additional activities are included.

**Iguazu is a concentrated nature section.** On day five, the group flies from Rio to Foz do Iguaçu. Day six is devoted to the [Brazilian waterfalls and Macuco Safari](/brazil/foz-do-iguacu/brazilian-iguazu-waterfalls-macuco-english/). Panoramic platforms reveal the falls from the Brazilian side, while the boat excursion offers a different experience close to the water. Macuco Safari operates within the national park; ordinarily, boat excursion tickets and park admission are sold separately. In this tour, however, both the excursion and tickets appear among the included services. The commercial package should explicitly confirm both components.

**São Paulo completes the itinerary.** After a flight on day seven, the group takes a [tour of Liberdade](/brazil/sao-paulo/liberdade-half-day-english/), the city's Japanese neighborhood. Day eight features a [half-day city tour](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-city-half-day-english/). Day nine is reserved for the airport transfer and departure, making it difficult to add a lengthy independent excursion without changing the schedule.

## How the 40+1 format differs from an individual trip

For a group of 40, time shared by all participants is a crucial resource. A delay boarding the bus, checking in for a flight or entering a hotel affects the entire sequence. Airport welcomes, lunch timing and buffers between transfers and departures therefore matter just as much as the sightseeing.

An English-speaking guide is listed for each stop. The stand-alone excursion modules are also designed to be led in English, which should be considered when assembling the group. **FOC means one complimentary place under the specified group price calculation**, not a blanket exemption from expenses for all travelers.

In Rio, the route covers city panoramas, neighborhoods and forest; in São Paulo, the focus is on a sightseeing drive and Liberdade. If a longer beach holiday or several days in national parks are priorities, compare [other Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) rather than expecting them from this nine-day itinerary.

## Pricing, accommodation and costs that must be distinguished

For the 40+1 group, the price is **$4,640 per person sharing a double room (DBL)** and **$7,140 for single occupancy (SGL)**. The offer table is headed "5-star hotels + services." However, the general list of exclusions separately says accommodation is not included unless it is specifically stated in the individual offer.

These terms contain a discrepancy, so it would be wrong to assume that particular five-star hotels are guaranteed within the published amounts. Before the program is agreed, hotel names, number of nights, room categories and the exact contents of the DBL/SGL rates must be confirmed in writing.

Expenses explicitly excluded include **international and domestic air tickets**, drinks with meals, insurance, visa fees where applicable, personal expenses, tips and additional events. No fixed arrival dates are given in the published itinerary. Domestic flight costs are not included in the stated $4,640/$7,140 amounts.

## Meals and themed evenings

Lunches are planned during several excursions, along with a group welcome dinner and meals in the hotels. The included-services list also names **Theme Party 1 in Rio** and **Theme Party 2 in Foz do Iguaçu**. Their precise dates and formats are not assigned in the day-by-day schedule.

For a group organizer, this means agreeing on the venue and time of each dinner around travel arrangements, then defining the content of each evening separately. Drinks are excluded. The phrase "Theme Party" alone does not justify promising a particular show, performers or exclusive venue.

## What to confirm before booking the group

Start by fixing airports and flights on the Rio–Foz do Iguaçu–São Paulo route, then arrange the excursions around them. At [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), access to viewing trails and boat activities depends on current park rules and water conditions. Participants should have rain protection, non-slip footwear and a way to keep electronics dry. Comfortable walking shoes will also be useful in Rio and São Paulo.

The support arrangements and logistics for a large group deserve particular attention: meeting points, luggage handling time, meals after late arrivals, language needs and individual restrictions. We can coordinate these details when preparing the group itinerary, based on the actual list of services.

## Frequently asked questions about the group itinerary

### How many people is this program designed for?

Pricing is based on 40 participants and one FOC complimentary place. The per-person price applies to that group size, and different numbers require a separate calculation.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. Flights between Rio, Foz do Iguaçu and São Paulo are excluded, as are international tickets.

### Are five-star hotels guaranteed at the quoted price?

Not yet definitively. The pricing table mentions a five-star hotel package, whereas the general exclusions include accommodation unless separately agreed. The exact offer and hotels must be confirmed.

### What languages are provided?

English-speaking guides are specified for the listed transfers and excursions. No other guiding language is stated.

### Can we add another excursion independently?

Additional activities incur extra costs. Whether they can be fitted in depends on the group's timetable, flights and the free portions of the sightseeing days.

## Five days in Rio for New Year: Copacabana, Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain

**The entire itinerary takes place in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), without domestic flights or hotel changes.** Over five days and four nights, guests celebrate New Year on Copacabana, visit the city's two main viewpoints, explore historic neighborhoods and enjoy a free day for independent activities.

This format is ideal for travelers primarily interested in Rio's New Year atmosphere. For waterfalls, choose the [seven-day itinerary including Iguazu](/brazil/tour/rio-iguazu-new-year-7-days/). If you want three nights on another stretch of coast after Iguazu, consider the [ten-day program with Búzios](/brazil/tour/brazil-new-year-rio-iguazu-buzios-10-days/).

## The New Year section of the trip

On day one, guests are met at the airport, transferred as a group and checked into their hotel. The remaining time can be spent walking beside the ocean.

Day two includes a visit to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado. The train climbs through Tijuca Forest, and the summit offers panoramic views of bays, beaches and city districts. In the evening, travelers welcome the New Year on Copacabana. White clothing, music and fireworks over the water are hallmarks of the celebrations; a separate New Year's dinner is not included in the base package.

Day three features the cable car via Urca to Sugarloaf Mountain and Rio's historic center. Guanabara Bay and the coastline are particularly visible from the viewpoint. In the center, attention turns to historic façades and Candelária Church. During the holiday period, the order of excursions may change because of traffic or attraction operating hours.

**For Copacabana, plan your route back to the hotel before the celebration.** Municipal street closures and special public transport arrangements are established separately for each New Year. The plan used in previous years is not necessarily the timetable for the next celebration.

## Day four: choose your own activities

No compulsory excursions are scheduled for day four. You can spend the day in Rio or choose one of the optional outings:

- A leisurely walk through the Botanical Garden.
- A guided tour of the Rocinha neighborhood.
- A helicopter flight or hang-gliding, weather and health permitting.
- A boat excursion to the bays of [Angra dos Reis](/brazil/place/angra-dos-reis/).

These are **alternative options**, not a set of activities all included in the base price. Services are selected and paid for separately. Day five ends with a transfer to Rio airport.

## Price and included services

| Item | According to the itinerary |
|---|---|
| Duration | 5 days / 4 nights |
| Overnight stays | Rio only |
| Free day | Day four |
| Price | From $2056 |

The price includes accommodation, group transfers, excursions and meals according to the tour conditions. International flights, optional excursions and drinks, tips and personal expenses are excluded. The hotel may be replaced with another of the same category.

During the South American summer, Rio can be hot with heavy showers. City sightseeing calls for comfortable footwear, light clothes, sun protection and a compact rain poncho. On New Year's Eve itself, expect very large crowds and restrictions on road traffic.

## Who will enjoy a short New Year stay in Rio

This tour suits travelers who want to see Rio's main panoramas, celebrate New Year beside the ocean and have a free day. It avoids spending holiday time on domestic flights, although it does not include a separate nature itinerary in other regions of Brazil.

To see [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), compare the [seven-day tour](/brazil/tour/rio-iguazu-new-year-7-days/); for a beach finale outside Rio, explore the [ten-day tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-new-year-rio-iguazu-buzios-10-days/).

## Frequently asked questions about the five-day tour

### Are all four nights spent in Rio?

Yes. The core program does not involve traveling to another resort.

### Is an excursion to Christ the Redeemer included?

Yes. Corcovado is part of the scheduled program, along with Sugarloaf Mountain.

### Do we have to visit Angra dos Reis?

No. This is a possible extra on the free day.

### Is a New Year's dinner included?

A separate restaurant dinner is not among the included services. The New Year's Eve celebration takes place on Copacabana.

## São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro in 11 days, October 2027

This trip is planned for **October 20–30, 2027**, lasting 11 days and 10 nights for a group of **22 participants**. The route begins in [São Paulo](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/), with four nights, then continues to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) for six nights. The first days focus on urban history and Paulista Avenue; in Rio, sightseeing includes Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and an introduction to the favelas, along with two free days.

This journey suits a group that wants to experience two very different Brazilian metropolises while leaving room for independent discoveries. There are **no visits to Iguazu Falls** and no long domestic flights across the country. The main practical questions concern the precise excursions, the terms at the two hotels and the airport transfer on the final day.

## Why the journey starts in São Paulo

Airport reception and a transfer with an English-speaking guide are scheduled for October 20. Accommodation is planned at **Ibis São Paulo Paulista, Standard room + BB**, or a similar hotel. The room arrangement includes breakfast.

October 21 features a [four-hour tour of São Paulo and Paulista Avenue](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-paulista-four-hours/); October 22 brings a four-hour visit to the historic center. These reveal different aspects of the city. Paulista Avenue presents the modern business district, while the historic center offers older architecture and public squares.

**October 23 is a free day.** Guests may choose their own walk, museum or park, but tickets, guides or a particular optional event are not automatically included in the price. The group should ideally decide in advance whether this day will remain independent or require an additional agreed excursion.

On October 24, an overland transfer to Rio is scheduled with an English-speaking guide. This is a separate travel and check-in day, not a fourth excursion in São Paulo.

## What is planned in Rio

From October 24 to 30, the group is based in Rio. The listed accommodation is **Ibis Copacabana Posto 5, Standard room + BB**, or a similar property. The ocean and city are both within reach, with sightseeing divided into three distinct days.

| Date | Activity |
|---|---|
| October 25 | [Sugarloaf Mountain](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/sugarloaf-cable-car-four-hours/) |
| October 26 | [Corcovado](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/corcovado-four-hours/) |
| October 27 | [Favela tour](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/favela-community-four-hours/) |
| October 28–29 | Free time |

Each of the three included excursions lasts **four hours** and is led by an English-speaking guide. The itinerary explicitly includes admission tickets for Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado. The favela visit is an organized guided excursion, not permission for travelers to visit any neighborhood unaccompanied; its particular format and route should be considered separately.

Free days on October 28 and 29 allow time for beach relaxation, neighborhood walks or independent cultural activities. The itinerary mentions Arpoador, Santa Teresa and Lapa as possibilities. These are ideas for free time, **not prepaid optional excursions**. Beach plans should take into account the weather and sea conditions on the day.

## DBL and SGL rates: what is covered

For the group of 22, the net rates are **$1,122 per person in DBL** and **$1,642 in SGL**. These combine the itinerary services and accommodation.

| Per person | Price |
|---|---:|
| Services, excursions, transfers | $526 |
| DBL accommodation | $596 |
| SGL accommodation | $1,116 |
| Full DBL package | $1,122 |
| Full SGL package | $1,642 |

The package includes private transfers and the listed excursions, an English-speaking guide, **ten nights'** accommodation with breakfast, and admission tickets for the attractions specified in the itinerary. Flights, lunches, dinners, extra excursions, tips and personal expenses are paid for separately.

We may substitute similar hotels for the listed properties. The rates apply to this particular group and are not universal prices for an individual trip. When comparing DBL and SGL, the actual room category agreed for the accommodation matters as well as the difference in price.

## Why the final transfer needs clarification

The schedule lists a transfer on October 30 from the hotel to **GRU airport (Guarulhos, São Paulo)**, even though the last six nights and days nine and ten are spent in Rio. This is a significant itinerary detail: the departure airport and practical route back from Rio must be confirmed before booking international tickets.

Do not assume this means a short transfer to one of Rio's airports. If the group really departs from GRU, the journey to São Paulo requires a separate time and transport plan with a sufficient buffer. If the international flight leaves from Rio, the last day's itinerary should be agreed accordingly. **Confirming the airport protects the group against a missed connection** and an unplanned journey.

## How this trip differs from other Brazil programs

This itinerary centers on two cities, cultural excursions and free time in Rio. Travelers seeking more varied natural landscapes should separately compare the [Brazil tour catalog](/brazil/tour/). Groups that prioritize waterfalls can consider the [nine-day Rio–Iguazu–São Paulo group itinerary](/brazil/tour/rio-iguazu-sao-paulo-group-9-days/), which covers three cities and a nature section, but has a different meal package and does not specify ten nights' accommodation on the same terms.

The October trip offers more time on Rio's coastline: three sightseeing days are followed by two free days. When choosing, the actual schedule and accommodation pattern are more important than a simple comparison of "11 versus 9 days."

## Frequently asked questions about the October tour

### What dates is the program planned for?

**October 20–30, 2027.** It lasts 11 days and 10 nights, with four nights in São Paulo and six in Rio.

### How much are double and single occupancy?

The net per-person rate for the group of 22 is $1,122 in DBL or $1,642 in SGL. Services and accommodation under the stated program are included.

### What is included on free days?

Accommodation with breakfast remains part of the package. Excursions and other paid activities are not automatically added to free days.

### Why is GRU airport listed at the end?

That is what the current itinerary specifies. Because the final nights are spent in Rio, the October 30 transfer plan and actual international departure airport must be agreed before tickets are purchased.

### Can the hotels be changed?

The itinerary allows similar replacement hotels. Exact names, categories and confirmed prices are fixed when booking.

## Southern Brazil in 12 days: from Rio and Iguazu to canyons and the ocean

Brazil is difficult to capture in a single kind of journey. In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), visitors climb to panoramic viewpoints; around [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), they see immense waterfalls; in [Gramado](/brazil/place/gramado/), they stroll along well-kept streets among the hills; and [Florianópolis](/brazil/place/florianopolis/) reveals a coastline with very different kinds of beaches.

The [12-day southern Brazil tour](/brazil/tour/southern-brazil-rio-iguazu-gramado-florianopolis-12-days/) connects these destinations across several regions. It is a **12-day, 11-night** private journey, priced from **$8761**. Alongside famous landmarks, the program includes a glass platform above a gorge, trekking near canyons and a sunrise hot-air balloon flight.

A defining feature of the itinerary is its combination of long-distance flights and overland transfers. **The domestic Rio–Iguazu–Porto Alegre flight routing is not included in the tour price**; the "Not included" section gives an indicative cost **from $600**. This matters when comparing it with journeys whose air tickets are already part of the package.

## Days 1–3: Rio, Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado

The journey begins in Rio, with an airport transfer, hotel check-in and rest. The following days introduce the city's iconic views from Sugarloaf Mountain, Corcovado and the Christ the Redeemer statue. From above, visitors can see bays, beaches, mountains and urban districts nestled between steep slopes and the ocean.

This opening reveals Rio from more than its beaches. It is a helpful introduction before traveling onward, giving visitors a broader understanding of the geography of this large coastal city.

## Days 4–6: Iguazu and onward to Gramado

On day four, the route moves to [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The program includes waterfall excursions and a boat trip, with time in the Foz do Iguaçu area to discover different viewpoints. The principal sightseeing geography described here is on the Brazilian side; the two sides of the border should not be combined in an individual day's description without a confirmed visit.

The journey then continues south via Porto Alegre. In [Gramado](/brazil/place/gramado/) and [Canela](/brazil/place/canela/), visitors explore hill towns, parks and viewpoints. The scenery changes gradually: after the ocean and tropical vegetation, cooler uplands and canyons take center stage.

On day seven, guests visit the Skyglass platform suspended over Canela's gorge. The group then travels toward Praia Grande and the canyons of southern Brazil.

## Days 7–8: canyons, a glass viewpoint and a balloon flight

The mountain canyons around Praia Grande and Cambará do Sul are known for their steep cliffs and broad valleys, where clouds rise from below. The route includes viewpoints, walks and stops in natural areas.

On day eight, **a hot-air balloon flight at sunrise is scheduled for early morning**, followed by travel to a national park, several relatively short hikes and a picnic overlooking the gorges. These activities depend on suitable weather. Their precise order may be adjusted, but the planned experiences remain part of the tour program.

If hiking is your main interest, compare this journey with [adventure tours in Brazil](/interests/adventure/tours/brazil/). It offers canyons and trekking, but a substantial part of the trip takes place by vehicle and includes urban sightseeing.

## Days 9–12: Florianópolis and time by the ocean

After the canyons, travelers head to [Florianópolis](/brazil/place/florianopolis/). A tour of the city and island is planned for day ten. Sights include November 15 Square, the Cruz e Sousa Palace, the historic Hercílio Luz Bridge and the Lagoa da Conceição neighborhood.

Day eleven is free for the beach, walks or relaxing by the ocean. Day twelve includes breakfast and a transfer to Florianópolis airport.

This conclusion suits travelers who would appreciate an unscheduled day after many transfers. The island offers different beaches, ranging from quieter bays to stretches of coastline with surfable waves.

## Cost and included services

| Item | Terms |
|---|---|
| Duration | 12 days, 11 nights |
| Starting price | $8761 |
| Format | Private |
| Domestic flights | Separate, from $600 |

The rate includes accommodation according to the itinerary, excursions with a **Russian-speaking guide in Rio and Iguazu**, English-speaking support for the remainder of the route, and transfers with a driver.

Optional excursions, the Rio–Iguazu–Porto Alegre flights, and food and drinks during transfers are outside the base price. Hotels may be replaced with others of the same category when necessary; the order of visits may also change while the overall program is maintained.

Compare this route with [other Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) and [beach holidays](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/brazil/). For more time by the ocean, choose a different balance of days. For waterfalls, viewpoints and natural landscapes, these experiences account for much of this trip.

## Frequently asked questions about southern Brazil

### How long is the journey?

**12 days and 11 nights**, from arrival in Rio to departure from Florianópolis.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. The Rio–Iguazu–Porto Alegre flights are paid for separately, **from $600**.

### Where is the hot-air balloon flight scheduled?

It is planned for early morning on day eight, around the canyons near Praia Grande. Suitable weather is important.

### Will there be time for a beach holiday?

Yes. Day eleven in Florianópolis is free. Earlier in the journey, the beaches and city of Rio give way to waterfalls, mountains and canyons.
